brief_context: Discussed as an island nation that cannot act in isolation.
brief_extract:
INTERNATIONAL OUTLOOK
by MARY GEORGE, MBE, Director EAW

Josephine Appiah and other overseas students at a Christmas party in Miss George's flat

'O, it's a snug little island
A right little, tight little island'

MUCH water has flowed under our bridges into the seas that surround us since Thomas Dibdin wrote those lines some 150 years ago. Today we in Britain can no longer sit snug and tight on our island and ignore what goes on beyond our shores. Whether we like it or not we have to think and act internationally if we are to fulfil our responsibilities within the Commonwealth, assist towards the solution of many world problems and keep ourselves economically viable.

location_standardised: Compton Place, Eastbourne, East Sussex, England, United Kingdom
brief_context: Home of the Dukes of Devonshire.
brief_extract: The impressive lay-out of the town is due chiefly to the fact that it has been the home of the Dukes of Devonshire, who did much to make Eastbourne what it is today, planning it long before Town and Country Planning Acts were ever heard of. The house of the Dukes is known as Compton Place and the late King George V and Queen Mary came often to stay there together with the late King George VII, the Queen Mother and the present Queen and her sister when they were children. One of the places of interest in Eastbourne is the Belle Tout lighthouse which is on the sheer cliff edge near to the famed Seven Sisters, which are in fact seven sheer cliffs with valleys between.

A town rich in history
Eastbourne, contrary to its appearance, is rich in history, not only within the town but in the surrounding beautiful Sussex countryside. Originally the town itself consisted of three small mediaeval villages and one of these was known as East Bourne, named after the stream which rose in Motcombe Gardens and ran through the village to the sea. A considerable amount still remains of the old village and the area is known locally as Old Town.

Four miles from Eastbourne in the other direction is Pevensey Castle, which was originally the Roman fortress known as Anderida, and on the walls of which Pevensey Castle was built by William the Conqueror, who landed at nearby Norman's Bay exactly 900 years ago. brief_context: The egg became a symbol in Mediterranean countries.
brief_extract: The chocolate Easter egg introduced in Victorian times may have been the extent of our experience but the significance of the egg is much wider than this. The ancient Chinese offered eggs as a thanksgiving at Spring festivals, and in some Mediterranean countries the egg became the symbol of the death and resurrection of the god in the first "mystery" religions. Because it signified birth and rebirth the egg was believed to have magical power to ensure fertility.

brief_extract:
Co-operation

by MARY GEORGE, MBE, Companion IEE,
DIRECTOR EAW

Standards of Goods
Sometimes the representatives of the EAW also speak on behalf of the Women's Advisory Committee of BSI. This committee known as the WAC was established in 1951 and has on it representatives of 28 leading women's organisations in the United Kingdom including, of course, the EAW. This powerful umbrella organisation advises BSI on the need for new standards for consumer articles or the revision of existing standards, and represents the needs and opinions of the ordinary shopper when standards are being drafted.

brief_context: Referenced in relation to the Scottish Accident Prevention Council.
brief_extract:
Safety
Safety is one of the prime concerns of the EAW and the WAC, both of whom have close links with the Royal Society for the Prevention of Accidents (RoSPA). Representation on the RoSPA Home Safety Committee and its Scottish equivalent the Scottish Accident Prevention Council gives the EAW further opportunities of representing the user's point of view on a national scale and of correcting any misapprehensions regarding electricity in the home. The EAW's stand at the Annual Home Safety Conference and Exhibition brings our work of electrical education to the attention of many of the delegates who come from local authorities.

brief_context: Trade with the Orient introduced caned chairs and lacquered furniture.
article_title: Who's been sitting in my chair?
brief_extract: The Great Fire gave scope for new furnishing styles because new furniture was needed for the new brick houses with smaller rooms which were replacing the timber framed houses which had been burnt down. Trade with the Orient also introduced caned chairs and lacquered furniture. By the reign of George I mahogany had become the fashionable wood and its strength and rich colour inspired many great cabinet makers such as William Kent and Thomas Chippendale.

brief_context: Mentioned as an influence on British furniture design styles.
brief_extract: Today, design and construction are once more united. Today, too, international trends influence furniture design and Scandinavian styles have had a marked effect on British furniture. The wood most widely used for Scandinavian-inspired furniture is teak and also afrormosia, a wood of the same family.

brief_context: Mentioned regarding differences in table setting methods
brief_extract: Matters discussed included suitable soiling material and standard place settings of china and cutlery. Catering students from the Borough Polytechnic and chairside assistants at the Eastman Dental Clinic attended three-lesson courses at 25 Foubert’s Place and a similar course was organised in Oxford at the request of the wife of the Principal of Jesus College for the wives of post-graduates at the college. Many of these people came from overseas and some are quite unaccustomed to electricity.

brief_context: The country where the gyrator was invented in the 1930s.
brief_extract: It was not till 1934 that all of the washing machine was enclosed in a neat cabinet. brief_extract:
I am a sixth form student
and have to write a thesis on the development of
types of cookers. It is very difficult to ascertain the exact year
in which the first electric cooker was produced,
but at the 1891-2 Electrical Exhibition at the
Crystal Palace, electricity was used to prepare
the lunch. In spite of the fact that the chicken
served at this meal was not perfectly cooked,
the luncheon marked the beginning of electric
cooking.

Brains Trusts have provided for discussing a problem from several angles. Special 'Wise Consumer' events in the branches are as follows:
(1) Stockton arranged for groups of members to study the local shopping background of various commodities, and each group reported to its leader who prepared a report listing the pros and cons. This study entailed the actual purchase of items on which opinions were given, and this was a really practical exercise revealing points relating to convenience, economy, saving of time, service and maintenance, as well as value for money.

Members first toured the automatic screw machine department and saw the inspection and quality con- trol sections for all parts used in the final assembly; next the jig and tool maintenance section; and then the injection moulding section which produces the polystyrene meter and time switch covers. brief_context: The regions for which domestic watthour meters are produced.

brief_extract: After the coil winding section came the next stage in motor assembly on a conveyor line producing 10,000 motor coils per week; and then the motor final assembly where the small synchronous motor is fitted to all time switches, etc., prior to package and dispatch. In the meter test section and assembly domestic watthour meters are made for Scottish areas, and members saw the laboratory test equipment where stringent quality control tests are conducted. In the main time switch sub-assembly and movement assembly sections conveyor line production gives a weekly production of 9,000 to 10,000 time switches.

article_title: VISIT TO C.E.G.B. RESEARCH LABORATORIES, LEATHERHEAD
brief_extract:
S. ROSS, London

The laboratories carry out research on the prob-
lems arising in the generation, transmission and dis-
tribution of electricity, and the organisation has five
divisions: High Voltage, Physics (including control
and communications); Engineering (electrical, mech-
anical and civil), Chemistry and Biology, and
Materials. The following items illustrate some of the work
undertaken: the testing of 275 kV overhead line
spacers for the prevention of conductor clashing; in-
vestigations of the aerodynamics of turbine blade
erosion; the use of a low-speed wind tunnel for in-
vestigating the performance aspects of cooling towers;
an exhibit in the Biology Section showing the fresh
water fauna found in rivers near power stations, the
analysis of insect life-cycles, the fish found in a warm
water effluent channel and experimental apparatus
for investigating the effect of temperature on insect
life-cycles and growth; a simulated cable trench used
to investigate the characteristics of more economic
loss-free plastic pipes for the water-cooling of 275
kV cables; a demonstration in the High Voltage
Laboratory to simulate switching surges which can
occur on the Grid system.
